headline: Wild's Brock Faber back at practice after recovery from fractured skull
take:
ESPN reports that Minnesota Wild defenseman Brock Faber has returned to practice after a fractured skull, a step toward his regular season debut, which the injury delayed.

The Wild don't look like a team waiting on a rescue. MIN sits at 11-3-3 with 25 points in 17 games, and the underlying numbers back that up. Expected goals, a measure of the quality of shots taken and allowed, put MIN at 57.4 percent of the total so far this season, and 54 percent at five-on-five. The special teams are sound too: the power play generates 0.91 expected goals per game, and the penalty kill allows just 0.64.

The more interesting wrinkle is that MIN has scored 8.8 fewer goals than its chances would suggest, while goalies have saved 10.1 more than expected (goals saved above expected, the gap between goals allowed and what the shot quality predicted). Those two roughly offset, so the record looks earned rather than lucky. Faber's return adds a defenseman to a group already controlling play, which matters most if the shooting finally catches up.
